在發展過程中，齊塔拉琴吸收了鄰近地區，特別是土耳其巴格拉瑪琴的特徵，形成了獨特的: In the course of its development the tzouras took on features from neighbouring regions, especially from the Turkish bağlama, and so formed its own musical character. The standardisation of its string layout and tuning lets players present Greek folk music dependably. Over time the tzouras spread from the Greek mainland along the Mediterranean coast and became an important instrument of Greek traditional music and folk culture, carrying on the history of a meeting between Eastern and Western musical cultures.
齊塔拉琴在希臘傳統民謠中被廣泛使用。著名作品包括《希臘民謠組曲》，由民間音樂家編: The tzouras is widely used in Greek traditional folk song. Well-known works include the "Greek Folk Song Suite", compiled by folk musicians and usually written down formally in the middle of the 20th century, and traditional folk pieces such as "Songs of the Aegean", which have come down through performances by generations of musicians. The modern composer Mikis Theodorakis also wove tzouras elements into his works, joining a traditional instrument to a contemporary style.
齊塔拉琴琴身主要由木材製成，通常採用杉木或雲杉製作共鳴腔體以獲得最佳音響效果。琴: The tzouras body is made mainly of wood, usually fir or spruce for the soundbox, which gives the best sound. The neck and head are of a hard hardwood, which keeps the structure stable. The strings are high-tension steel, usually steel-wound, and give a bright, clear tone. The nut and bridge are of bone or hardwood, which helps to transmit the vibration of the strings. The tuning pegs are of wood or metal and control the tension for tuning.
齊塔拉琴起源於希臘，是一種承載悠久音樂傳統的弦樂器。其名稱源自土耳其的庫拉琴，反: The tzouras originated in Greece and is a string instrument carrying a long musical tradition. Its name comes from the Turkish cura, which reflects the mixing of instrument cultures in the eastern Mediterranean. As an instrument related to the bouzouki, the tzouras gradually established its own place in the development of Greek music. It comes in six-string and eight-string versions, and the six-string model has the same construction as the bouzouki, with three pairs of steel strings.
齊塔拉琴音色明亮清脆，具有典型的地中海弦樂器特徵。其鋼弦材質賦予樂器銳利而富有穿: The tzouras has a bright, clear timbre, typical of Mediterranean string instruments. Its steel strings give a sharp, carrying tone, with the range concentrated in the upper middle, lively and full of energy. Because the strings are paired, their resonances reinforce one another and produce full, rich overtones, which gives the tone more layers. Against the warm classical guitar the tzouras has more of a metallic quality, and against the bouzouki its tone is a little brighter and stronger. The design of the soundbox keeps the tone clearly defined while giving it enough volume to project, which suits playing indoors and lets it show its particular character in traditional Greek music.
齊塔拉琴（希臘語：τζουράς）是一種與布祖基琴相關的希臘弦樂器。其名稱源自土: The tzouras (Greek: τζουράς) is a Greek string instrument related to the bouzouki. Its name comes from the Turkish cura. It comes in six-string and eight-string versions. Similar instruments in Turkish culture are usually called bağlama. The six-string model has the same string arrangement and pitches as the six-string (three-course) bouzouki. There are three pairs of strings, tuned D3D4–A3A3–D4D4 or D4D3–A3A3–D4D4. The strings are made of steel.
